## Hands-on 3 – 8PTRZ uncorrected {#hands-on-3-8ptrz-uncorrected .smaller .output-8}

::: {.small}
The test of 8PTRZ with `correct = FALSE`. *IDE:* the chunk `reproduce-uncorrected`.
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# 8PTRZ: the replies with a greeting code, Hispanic against all other names
coded_replies <- original |>
  datawizard::data_filter(!is.na(ProperName)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic_name = grepl("^Hispanic", TreatmentGroup))
```

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
tab_8ptrz <- xtabs(~ hispanic_name + ProperName, data = coded_replies)
```

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
chisq.test(tab_8ptrz, correct = FALSE)
```

::: notes
Here the correction is switched off. The first two cells rebuild the table of 8PTRZ from the public file, whichever analyst you reproduced, and print nothing, and the third runs the same test with correct equals false. The first line of the printout loses the words about the correction, and the statistic rises from fourteen point two six five to fourteen point nine five. The conclusion does not change, since both values are far beyond any threshold, but only the corrected value matches the record. In the IDE workspace the same test sits in the chunk after the five tabs of Task 3.
:::

## Hands-on 3 – 25N5D uncorrected {#hands-on-3-25n5d-uncorrected .smaller .output-8}

::: {.small}
The counts of 25N5D, then the test with `correct = FALSE`.
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# 25N5D: the delivered emails, Hispanic against white names
counts_25n5d <- original |>
  datawizard::data_filter(!is.na(Response_Dichotomous) & !grepl("^black", TreatmentGroup)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic_name = grepl("^Hispanic", TreatmentGroup),
                          greeted = Response_Dichotomous == 1 & ProperName %in% 1) |>
  datawizard::data_summary(greetings = sum(greeted), emails = n(), by = "hispanic_name")
```

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
prop.test(counts_25n5d$greetings, counts_25n5d$emails, correct = FALSE)
```

::: {.fragment .small}
Without the correction: `r fmt_num(chi_plain, 2)` and `r fmt_num(prop_plain, 2)`; only the corrected values match the record.
:::

::: notes
The same for 25N5D. The first cell counts the greetings and the delivered emails for the Hispanic and the white names in one pipe and prints nothing, and the second tests the two proportions without the correction. [advance] The statistic rises from thirteen point six eight three to fourteen point three three. Both analysts reported the corrected value without asking for it, because the two functions apply the correction by default, and a report that says only that a chi-square test was run fits both numbers. A reproduction therefore needs the code, or at least every default and every coding on which the code relied.
:::
